You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The test `testEncodingInputStream` fails because the encoding is not passed correctly to some ArchiveInputStream implementations in the `ArchiveStreamFactory`. According to the current bug report, `ArchiveStreamFactory` fails to pass on the encoding when creating streams for several archive types such as ArjArchiveInputStream, CpioArchiveInputStream, DumpArchiveInputStream, JarArchiveInputStream, and JarArchiveOutputStream.

Inspecting the code of `ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream(String, InputStream)`:
- For some archive types (Arj, Cpio, Dump, Jar), the code branches check if the `entryEncoding` field is not null. If it is not null, it calls the constructor with the encoding, else without it.
- The encoding is stored in `entryEncoding`, which is also set during construction from the constructor parameter `encoding` or else is null.
- The setter `setEntryEncoding` also sets this field but may throw if overridden.
- However, there is a newer overload mentioned in the test signature `createArchiveInputStream(String, InputStream, String)`, which was not found or at least we could not get the code snippet for, but likely supposed to allow passing the encoding explicitly for this call.
- The existing method `createArchiveInputStream(String, InputStream)` relies on the stored field `entryEncoding` rather than an explicit parameter.
- The bug report and the test imply the encoding is not always correctly propagated on some streams due to either improper handling of the encoding parameter or lack of usage of the method allowing explicit encoding.
- The recent related issues hint that encoding support was added but broke immutability and thread-safety, indicating there might be subtle problems where encoding is stored or not used consistently.

Conclusion:
The root cause is that the `ArchiveStreamFactory#createArchiveInputStream` method that only accepts `(String, InputStream)` uses a field `entryEncoding` which may not be correctly set or updated to pass encoding to all relevant stream constructors. Also, the overloaded method that accepts encoding explicitly is either missing or not used properly. Therefore, the encoding is not propagated for certain streams, causing the test to fail.

The fix would be to ensure the explicit encoding parameter is used when creating ArchiveInputStream instances, or to synchronize the setting and usage of `entryEncoding` correctly in this factory to pass encoding consistently to all supported input streams.

Next, I should locate the `createArchiveInputStream(String, InputStream, String)` method or the usage of encoding parameter in the factory to see if it correctly propagates the encoding passed in the method call, which seems to be missing or inconsistent.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
